newsitem.title: USA: Dow slips after in-line economic data.
newsitem.headline: Dow slips after in-line economic data.

text.p: Dow industrials fell on Tuesday as investors took profits and a break from last week's record-setting rally although key economic data sparked no inflation fears.
In late morning trading, the Dow was down about 46 points to 7726. The Nasdaq composite opened lower but started to gather steam, trading up about 0.65 at 1433.
"I think it is basically selling on the news," said Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co.
"There is nothing to suggest it's inflationary and it's not a cause for concern," he said of the economic data.
The U.S. May Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 0.1 percent compared to the 0.2 percent rise economists expected. Housing starts were slightly weaker than expected, falling to a 1.397 million-unit rate.
Marshall Acuff, portfolio strategist at Smith Barney, said the industrial output data, up 0.4 percent, were stronger than expected and may be influencing the Dow's decline.

"I would guess they would sell off a bit on this kind of news. This type of announcement creates that excuse," he said. "But if the market is as strong as it appears then any weakness would be met by some buying support.
